name: Avalanche Peak
why: The only poled route to a summit in Arthur's Pass: 1,100 m straight up from the village to an 1,833 m top facing Mount Rolleston and the Crow Glacier.
book: Free, no permit. Arthur's Pass village is on SH73, 150 km from Christchurch; the TranzAlpine train stops there. Check the track and avalanche conditions at the visitor centre before you start.
water: Avalanche Creek in the forest; none above the bushline. Carry 2 litres.
dangers: Steep, rocky and exposed with sheer drops; people have died here. Do not go in poor visibility or high wind.
The final ridge is a narrow rock edge: if it is windy, icy or snowy, go back the way you came.
Avalanche-prone in winter and spring; take an ice axe and crampons in winter.
Do not leave the marked route between the two ridges: a hidden canyon blocks the way.
turnaround: If the weather is poor or you found the climb to the bushline hard, enjoy the view at the bushline and turn back there.

points.name: Avalanche Peak Track, Arthur's Pass village
points.note: Just north of the visitor centre, before the bridge over Avalanche Creek (737 m). The track climbs through mountain beech beside the creek's waterfalls.

points.name: Avalanche Peak summit
points.note: 1,833 m. Mount Rolleston and the Crow Glacier across the valley; kea are often here. Descend on Scotts Route, orange poles, towards Mount Cassidy.

points.name: Scotts Track road end
points.note: Scotts Track meets SH73 about 700 m west of the visitor centre, by the Devils Punchbowl car park.
